head/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats:120 — GO-9 runs `guard-yield.sh --check` against the repository's own `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, which this change never adds. The test is red on merge (exit 1, drift).
head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:17 — The floor snapshot (AC-1.5) skips whenever `origin/main` is not reachable. The bats workflow uses `actions/checkout` at the default fetch-depth 1 (bats-tests.yml:90), so `origin/main` is never present and FS-1…FS-4 never run in CI. On main itself the check compares the tree with itself. The "floor does not move" guarantee is therefore never enforced.
head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:45 — FS-3 and FS-4 (line 50) require `.claude/settings.json` hooks and the fence's whole pattern-id call-site list to match origin/main byte for byte. Neither is in floor.yaml. As permanent tests they fail every future PR that adds or changes a hook registration or adds a fence pattern, not just changes "during a cycle".
head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:504 — `destructive_start` takes only the first word of each statement, so a `sudo`-prefixed command (`sudo rm -rf ./x`, which the fence itself matches through `(sudo[[:space:]]+)?`) or an env-assignment prefix is not seen as destructive. Such FR-2-AMBIGUOUS, SP-1 and FR-MERGE-2 blocks are labelled likely false positives (verified: `sudo rm -rf ./x` gave likely_fp=1 and last_real_catch "none in window"), which understates real catches.
head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:2 — The new `paths:` scope (`**/*.sh`, `**/*.bats`, `.claude/scripts/**`, `.claude/hooks/**`) means the rule loads only when a shell file is touched. The hazard it covers is `git stash` typed through the Bash tool during skill execution, and its own origin incident (#555) involved Edit-tool NOTES.md updates. Neither of these touches a matching path, so the judgment rules (no `stash -k` with pre-commit, fsck before gc) drop out of exactly the sessions they were written for.
head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:10 — The header says "Both bats suites pin this file's sha256", but only guard-origins.bats has FLOOR_SHA256. floor-snapshot.bats has no pin and says so at its line 10.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:163 — `LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES` from the caller's environment overrides the suite's pre-registered `ab.arms[]` entry, and run-arms.sh never clears it. If it is exported once, every arm, including `baseline`, runs with the same toggles while still recording its own arm name. That silently invalidates the pre-registered comparison. run-arms.bats passes only because it unsets the variable itself.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:263 — The `rule_files` toggle succeeds (exit 0, evidence "removed: none present") when neither rule file exists in the pinned tree, and also when only one exists. The arm then runs as baseline, or partly as baseline. This contradicts the header contract at lines 64-66 ("a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never silently runs as its baseline)").
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:256 — If the `constraints.json` Karpathy filter's `jq` fails (no `.constraints` key, or a top-level array), the failure is swallowed by the `&& mv` list. The Karpathy rows stay in the sandbox, `constraints.json.tmp` is left behind, and nothing verifies the removal, despite the "verified absent" claim.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:93 — `usage()` still cuts the header at `sed -n '2,60p'`, but the header now runs to about line 80. `--help` stops mid-sentence at "recorded as source_commit (default: the prompt" and omits all the new toggle documentation.
head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:302 — The "too small to name" downgrade compares `abs(drop)` with the baseline spread, so a large recall gain (negative drop) together with one low trial is reported as "recall loss … change named". The rule documented at lines 22-23 is about a mean drop exceeding the spread; it should compare the signed drop.
head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:240 — The coverage check skips clean fixtures (`planted == 0`) even when they have fewer than `trials_required` trials, yet their refuted share still feeds the refuted-share rule. With `coverage_required: full`, a missing cell should make the result inconclusive.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:251 — Re-running an existing batch with the same source and model is allowed, but nothing skips or resumes completed trials. Every trial runs again and is appended to `<arm>/results.jsonl`, MANIFEST is overwritten (possibly with different arms or fixtures), and STATUS restarts at 0. arms-report.py then counts the duplicates toward coverage and the trial means.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:246 — `cleanup` kills only the `jobs -p` subshells. On SIGINT/SIGTERM the `execute-agent.sh`/`timeout`/`claude` grandchildren survive, keep spending model calls, and their sandboxes are never destroyed. The same cleanup also `rm -rf`s `.jobs/`, which deletes the exec logs the "no row written" error message tells the operator to read.
head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:132 — `! grep -q …` in the middle of a bats test never fails it, because `set -e` ignores negated commands. The checks that Karpathy text and the audit-delta paragraph are absent from the sandbox and system prompt (lines 132, 133, 152, 153, 166) can never fail. Use `run ! grep` or `grep … && false`.
head/evals/tests/arms-report.bats:132 — AR-6 is titled as testing the default output path `evals/results/arms-report-<date>.md`, but it asserts only three bad-argument exit codes. The default path is never tested.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:769 — The fixture dir is deleted at line 730 before the rebuild. On a later failure (no-secrets scan, missing template) only `pr-NN/` and the label files are removed. The previous build's `manifests/pr-NN.json`, both `tasks/*/…-pr-NN.yaml` files and the `corpus.tsv` row survive, and SHA256SUMS is not refreshed. The suites then glob tasks whose fixture no longer exists, contradicting "nothing kept".
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:295 — The "not a record fixture; refusing to overwrite" guard fires only when a `fixture.yaml` exists. Any other existing dir (for example the `pr-01` template, which has none) passes the guard and is `rmtree`d at line 730.
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:161 — Because of that, SC-6 ("a non-record fixture is refused") never reaches the refusal. It passes on a FileNotFoundError traceback after the script has already deleted the template's REVIEW-/AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:312 — Renamed binaries appear in numstat as `dir/{old => new}/f.bin`. `p.split(" => ")[-1].strip("{}")` produces `new}/f.bin`, so the binary is not excluded and is copied through the UTF-8 `redact()` path, which corrupts the fixture file.
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:69 — Bare `! cmd` lines in the middle of the test (lines 69, 90, 91, 143) cannot fail it. The "previous-round section never read", "no secret key written", "c.sh not labelled" and "no corpus row" assertions are vacuous.
head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-kind-01.yml:6 — The comment says no suite, arm run or CI job picks this task up. However, `run-eval.sh` with no selector, or with `--skill reviewing-code`, matches `*.yml` and runs it. Only the suite glob excludes it.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 23 findings, verdict **CHANGES_REQUIRED**.

**Merge blocker:** the PR adds a CI step that runs `guard-yield.sh --check`, but it never commits the register file `grimoires/loa/guards.md`. Since `.gitignore` doesn't exclude that file, it is meant to be committed. I rebuilt a tree from the head files and ran the check: it exits 1, reporting drift, and only passes after the register is generated. The GO-9 test in `guard-origins.bats` fails for the same reason.

**Other important findings:**
- **Floor check never runs in CI.** The floor-snapshot tests skip whenever `origin/main` isn't available, and CI's default shallow checkout never fetches it. Two of those tests (FS-3, FS-4) would also fail any future PR that changes a hook registration or adds a fence pattern.
- **Control arms can be contaminated.** If `LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES` is set in the caller's shell, it overrides every arm's pre-registered toggles, including `baseline`'s, while each arm still records its own name. The `rule_files` toggle also reports success when there's nothing to remove, so that arm quietly runs as baseline.
- **Wrong verdicts in `arms-report.py`.** A large recall gain can be reported as a "recall loss" because the code uses `abs(drop)`. Clean fixtures with too few trials still count toward the refuted share instead of making the result inconclusive.
- **Batch runs:** re-running a batch appends duplicate results that the report then counts. Interrupting a run leaves the child agent processes running and still making model calls.
- **Corpus seeding:** a failed re-seed leaves stale manifests, task files and the corpus row behind. Any existing directory without a `fixture.yaml` (such as the `pr-01` template) gets deleted. Renamed binary files aren't detected as binary, so they're copied through text redaction and corrupted.
- **Smaller code bugs:** a `sudo`-prefixed destructive command is counted as a likely false positive in the guard yield. The stash-safety rule is now loaded only when shell files are touched, which misses the Bash-tool `git stash` sessions it was written for.
- **Tests that can't fail:** several assertions in `arm-toggles.bats` and `seed-corpus.bats` are written as `! grep …` mid-test, which bats never fails on. The SC-6 test passes only because the script crashes.

**What I could and couldn't run:** the PR snapshot holds only the touched files, so I ran things against rebuilt or stubbed trees. guard-yield's checks run cleanly, its yield numbers are right except for the `sudo` case, and the origin map lines up with the fence and validator markers and the floor list. `cycle-ratio.bats` passes 6/6 and the sprint-kinds validator tests pass. Two subagents reviewed the eval harness and seeding code, and I re-read the key lines myself for their top claims. I couldn't run `run-arms.bats`, `execute-agent.bats` or check the `pr-11`…`pr-18` fixtures, because they depend on files outside the PR.
